answer: Time-locked attention ledger. Each identity accrues weight only by completing unpredictable micro-tasks at dawn, when a rotating validator set publishes fresh work. Weight is non-transferable and decays without daily participation. To impersonate N agents, an attacker must staff N concurrent human workstreams, paying real labor hours rather than capital. A jade seal commits each day's ledger root; forged entries fail cross-validation. The garden of active identities stays small and costly to fake.
